title: The Medically Sick Child: Shock, Fever, Seizures, SIDS
next: Chapter 44, Lesson 4: Abuse, trauma, burns and children with special needs

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already treat shock with position, oxygen and warmth, and you know infant and child CPR. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize shock in a child and give weight-based IV fluid by BC's rules
  2. Handle fever, seizures, low blood sugar and poisoning
  3. Know BC's child CPR rules, and support a family after an infant death

Textbook: Chapter 44, PDF pages 3793–3838
slides.say: Welcome back. Today is about the medically sick child. As EMRs, you already treat shock by laying the patient down, giving oxygen and keeping them warm, and you know infant and child CPR. As a PCP, you add vascular access and fluids sized by weight, plus new drugs for fever and nausea, each with its own age limits. And you'll make more decisions: is this child compensating, or about to crash? We'll cover three things: shock and BC's fluid rules for children; fever, seizures, low sugar and poisoning; and BC's child CPR rules, with the hardest call of all, a sudden infant death.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。今天讲内科急症的患儿。作为 EMR，你们已经会处理休克：让病人躺平、给氧、保暖，也会婴儿和儿童 CPR。作为 PCP，你多了血管通路和按体重计算的补液，还有治疗发热和恶心的新药，每种都有各自的年龄限制。你还要做更多判断：这个孩子是在代偿，还是快要垮了？今天讲三件事：休克和 BC 的儿童补液规则；发热、抽搐、低血糖和中毒；以及 BC 的儿童 CPR 规则，和最难的一种呼叫——婴儿猝死。

slides.title: Shock: children hide it, then crash
slides.body:
CompensatedBP still normalfast HR, cool hands and feet, slow refill
Decompensatedsystolic below 70 + 2 × agealtered appearance: arrest is close
  • Blood volume only about 70 mL/kg
  • Most common type in children: hypovolemic
slides.say: Shock means the tissues aren't getting enough oxygen and nutrients. Children compensate very well: they tighten their vessels and speed up the heart, so in compensated shock the blood pressure is normal. You'll see a fast heart rate, cool hands and feet, and slow capillary refill, while the child may still look fairly normal. Once the pressure falls below seventy plus two times the age, the child is in decompensated shock, and cardiac arrest isn't far away. Children have only about seventy millilitres of blood per kilogram, so a few days of vomiting and diarrhea, or a bleeding injury, can cause shock quickly.
slides.sayZh: 休克就是组织得不到足够的氧和营养。孩子代偿能力很强：收紧血管、加快心率，所以代偿期休克血压是正常的。你会看到心率快、手脚凉、毛细血管再充盈慢，而孩子看上去可能还挺正常。一旦血压掉到七十加两倍年龄以下，就是失代偿性休克，心跳骤停已经不远了。孩子每公斤体重只有大约七十毫升血，所以几天的呕吐腹泻，或者一处出血的伤，很快就能导致休克。

slides.title: Four kinds of shock in a child
slides.body:
TypeCluesFluid?
Hypovolemicvomiting, diarrhea, bleeding; dry mouth, sunken eyesyes: the mainstay
Distributivefever (sepsis), hives (anaphylaxis), weakness after injuryyes, first
Obstructivesudden onset, chest traumayes, then fix the cause
Cardiogenicheart disease, murmur, big liver, sweats with feedsone slow bolus; watch
slides.say: Children get the same four kinds of shock as adults. Hypovolemic is the most common: vomiting, diarrhea or bleeding, with a dry mouth and sunken eyes. Distributive shock comes from vessels that open too wide and leak; in children it's usually sepsis, so look for fever, but anaphylaxis and spinal cord injury cause it too. Obstructive shock starts suddenly, often after chest trauma. Fluid comes first for all three. Cardiogenic shock is different: a known heart problem, a murmur, an enlarged liver, or a baby who sweats while feeding. If you suspect it, the book says give one slow bolus, and stop if the breathing or saturation gets worse.
slides.sayZh: 孩子的休克和成人一样分四种。低血容量性最常见：呕吐、腹泻或出血，伴口干、眼窝凹陷。分布性休克是血管扩得太开又渗漏；在孩子身上多半是脓毒症，所以要找发热，不过过敏反应和脊髓损伤也会引起。梗阻性休克起病突然，常在胸部外伤之后。这三种都先补液。心源性休克不一样：有已知心脏病、杂音、肝大，或者婴儿吃奶时出汗。怀疑是心源性，书里说只慢慢给一次液体，一旦呼吸或血氧变差就停。

slides.title: IV access in a child
slides.body:
• Catheters: 20, 22 or 24 gauge
  • Sites: back of the hand, inside of the elbow, foot or ankle
  • Isotonic fluid only (normal saline); warm it if you can
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, then reassess; repeat if needed
  • Treat sugar separately: dextrose only for a confirmed low

Book: one failed IV in decompensated shock, then IO. BC EMR/PCP: no IO.
slides.say: Use a twenty, twenty-two or twenty-four gauge catheter. The back of the hand and the inside of the elbow are the usual sites, and in children the veins of the foot and ankle work too. Give isotonic fluid only, such as normal saline, warmed if possible, as a bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram, then reassess before you repeat. Treat sugar separately: give dextrose only for a confirmed low. The book says that in decompensated shock you make one IV attempt, then switch to an intraosseous needle. IO isn't in BC's EMR or PCP scope, so don't let repeated IV attempts hold up transport.
slides.sayZh: 用二十、二十二或二十四号套管针。常用部位是手背和肘窝，孩子还可以用足部和踝部的静脉。只给等渗液，比如生理盐水，能加温就加温，按每公斤二十毫升推注，复评后再决定是否重复。血糖另外处理：只有确认低血糖才给葡萄糖。书里说失代偿性休克时静脉只试一次，失败就改骨髓腔穿刺。骨髓腔通路不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内，所以别让反复扎针耽误转运。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: hypovolemia in a child
slides.body:
BC Hypovolemia protocol: same protocol, weight-based fluid

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Control external bleeding
  • Splint pelvis / fractures if indicated
  • Lay supine; keep warm
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%

PCP adds (en route or if delayed)

  • Vascular access
  • Bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL and after each bolus
  • TXA: not under 12 years

Example: 15 kg child → 300 mL bolus.
slides.say: BC's hypovolemia protocol is the same for children; what changes is the math. The left column is every licence level: control external bleeding, splint the pelvis or fractures if indicated, lay the child flat, keep them warm, and give oxygen to keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or higher. The right column is yours. En route, or if there's a delay, start vascular access and consider a bolus of twenty millilitres per kilogram, up to two litres, reassessing as you go. For a fifteen-kilogram child, that's three hundred millilitres. TXA is in the protocol too, but its monograph says not under twelve years.
slides.sayZh: BC 的低血容量规程对孩子也一样，变的是算法。左栏是所有执照级别：控制外出血，有指征时固定骨盆或骨折，让孩子平躺、保暖，给氧使血氧维持在九十四以上。右栏是你的：在转运途中，或现场有延误时，建立血管通路，考虑按每公斤二十毫升推注、最多两升，边给边复评。十五公斤的孩子就是三百毫升。规程里也有 TXA，但它的药物专论写明十二岁以下禁用。

slides.q: An 8-month-old (8 kg) has had vomiting and diarrhea for 2 days. She is lethargic, with cool feet and refill of 4 seconds. You're the PCP. Fluid plan?
options: 160 mL bolus en route, reassess, repeat if needed
Try one IV, then place an IO
slides.say: Let's try the math. An eight-month-old weighing eight kilograms has had vomiting and diarrhea for two days. She's lethargic, with cool feet and a capillary refill of four seconds. You're the PCP. What's your fluid plan? A, a five hundred millilitre bolus, then reassess. B, a one hundred sixty millilitre bolus en route, then reassess and repeat if needed. C, two litres, the protocol maximum. D, try one IV, then place an IO. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来算一算。一个八个月、八公斤的婴儿呕吐腹泻两天，精神萎靡，脚凉，毛细血管再充盈四秒。你是 PCP，补液方案是什么？A，推注五百毫升，再复评；B，途中推注一百六十毫升，复评，需要时重复；C，两升，规程上限；D，试一次静脉，然后做骨髓腔穿刺。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Twenty millilitres per kilogram times eight kilograms is one hundred sixty millilitres. Give it en route, reassess, and repeat if she still shows signs of shock. A is about three times her dose, and C is an adult-sized maximum, not a target. D follows the book, but IO isn't in BC's EMR or PCP scope; keep transporting and keep trying for IV access en route.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。每公斤二十毫升乘以八公斤，就是一百六十毫升。途中给，复评，仍有休克表现就重复。A 大约是她剂量的三倍；C 是成人尺度的上限，不是目标量。D 是书上的做法，但骨髓腔通路不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内；继续转运，途中再争取静脉通路。

slides.title: Too slow, too fast
slides.body:
• Slow heart in a child = hypoxia until proven otherwise
  • First fix: airway, oxygen, ventilation
  • HR < 60 with poor perfusion: start CPR (BC)
  • Sinus tachycardia: fever, pain, fear, dehydration; rate varies
  • SVT: fixed rate, no clear P waves; infant > 220, child > 180

The book's adenosine and amiodarone are not on BC's exam drug list.
slides.say: Rhythm problems in children usually have another cause. A slow heart rate most often means hypoxia, so the first fix is always the airway, oxygen and ventilation. BC's child CPR protocol says start compressions if the heart rate is under sixty with poor perfusion. Fast rates are common. Sinus tachycardia comes from fever, pain, fear or dehydration, and the rate varies from minute to minute; treat the cause. Supraventricular tachycardia, or SVT, has a fixed rate, usually over two hundred twenty in infants or one hundred eighty in children, without clear P waves. An infant with SVT may just have fed poorly for days. The book's adenosine and amiodarone aren't BC exam drugs.
slides.sayZh: 孩子的心律问题通常另有原因。心率慢最常见的原因是缺氧，所以第一步永远是气道、给氧和通气。BC 的儿童 CPR 规程说，心率低于六十且灌注差，就开始按压。心率快很常见。窦性心动过速来自发热、疼痛、害怕或脱水，心率会一阵一阵地变；治病因。室上性心动过速（SVT）心率固定，婴儿通常超过二百二十，儿童超过一百八十，看不到清楚的 P 波。婴儿 SVT 可能只表现为几天吃奶不好。书里的腺苷和胺碘酮不是 BC 考纲药物。

slides.title: Child and infant CPR in BC
slides.body:
ItemBC rule
Ratio30:2 one rescuer; 15:2 two rescuers
Newborn (to 28 days)3:1; no AED
Start CPRno pulse, or HR < 60 with poor perfusion
Pulse checkbrachial in infants
AED padschild pads 0–8 years; adult pads if none
Alone, unwitnessed5 cycles (about 2 min) before the AED

"30:2 for everyone" is the adult rule only.
slides.say: Lock in BC's child and infant CPR rules, because the exam is strict. In BC, a child is from one year to puberty. One rescuer uses thirty to two; two rescuers use fifteen to two. Thirty to two for everyone is the adult rule only. A newborn, up to twenty-eight days old, gets three to one, with no AED. Start CPR if there's no pulse, or if the heart rate is under sixty with poor perfusion. Check an infant's pulse at the brachial artery. Use child pads up to eight years, or adult pads if that's all you have. And alone at an unwitnessed arrest, do five cycles, about two minutes, before the AED.
slides.sayZh: 要把 BC 的儿童和婴儿 CPR 规则记牢，因为考试很严。在 BC，儿童指一岁到青春期。单人按压通气比三十比二，双人十五比二；「一律三十比二」只是成人规则。新生儿（出生二十八天内）是三比一，不用 AED。没有脉搏，或心率低于六十且灌注差，就开始 CPR。婴儿查肱动脉。八岁以下用儿童电极片，没有就用成人电极片。一个人遇到无人目击的骤停，先做五个循环、约两分钟，再上 AED。

slides.title: Fever, and the baby under 2 months
slides.body:
• Fever is a symptom; its height doesn't show how sick
  • Under 2 months with fever over 38°C: transport, however well
  • Danger: stiff neck, bulging fontanelle, purple non-blanching spots
  • Assume bacterial meningitis: mask yourself and the child
  • No aspirin for children (Reye syndrome)

BC: ASA is contraindicated in children with viral symptoms.
slides.say: Fever is common, usually viral, and it's a symptom, not the disease. The number on the thermometer doesn't tell you how sick the child is. The exception is the young infant: any baby under two months with a temperature over thirty-eight degrees needs transport, however well they look. Watch for a stiff neck, a bulging fontanelle, or small purple spots that don't fade when pressed, which can mean meningococcal infection. Treat suspected meningitis as bacterial, wear a mask with eye protection, and mask the child. And never give children aspirin; it's linked to Reye syndrome.
slides.sayZh: 发热很常见，多半是病毒引起，它是症状，不是病本身。体温计上的数字说明不了孩子病得多重。例外是小婴儿：两个月以下的宝宝只要体温超过三十八度，不管看起来多好都要转运。注意颈部僵硬、囟门膨隆，或按压不褪色的紫色小点，这可能是脑膜炎球菌感染。怀疑脑膜炎就按细菌性处理，戴带护目的口罩，也给孩子戴口罩。还有，绝不给孩子用阿司匹林，它和瑞氏综合征有关。

slides.q: A 2-year-old (12 kg) has a temperature of 39.6°C and is otherwise well. Using BC's ibuprofen monograph, which dose fits?
slides.say: Here's a PCP dosing question. A two-year-old weighing twelve kilograms has a temperature of thirty-nine point six degrees and is otherwise well. Using BC's ibuprofen monograph, which dose fits? A, sixty milligrams by mouth, five milligrams per kilogram. B, one hundred twenty milligrams by mouth, ten milligrams per kilogram. C, A S A, one hundred sixty milligrams by mouth. D, four hundred milligrams, the adult dose. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 一道 PCP 剂量题。一个两岁、十二公斤的孩子体温三十九点六度，其他情况良好。按 BC 布洛芬药物专论，哪个剂量合适？A，口服六十毫克，每公斤五毫克；B，口服一百二十毫克，每公斤十毫克；C，阿司匹林一百六十毫克口服；D，四百毫克，成人剂量。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. For fever, a PCP indication, BC's pediatric ibuprofen dose is five milligrams per kilogram under thirty-nine degrees and ten milligrams per kilogram at thirty-nine or above. At thirty-nine point six, that's ten times twelve, or one hundred twenty milligrams, with a daily maximum of forty milligrams per kilogram. A is the dose for a lower temperature. C is wrong: ASA is contraindicated in children with viral symptoms. D is an adult dose and far too much for twelve kilograms.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。退热是 PCP 的适应证，BC 儿童布洛芬剂量是：体温低于三十九度每公斤五毫克，三十九度及以上每公斤十毫克。三十九点六度，就是十乘十二，一百二十毫克，每日上限每公斤四十毫克。A 是体温较低时的剂量。C 错，有病毒症状的儿童禁用阿司匹林。D 是成人剂量，对十二公斤的孩子太多了。

slides.title: Sleepy, seizing, or low sugar
slides.body:
• Altered LOC: think AEIOU-TIPS; always check glucose
  • BC: treat BGL < 4.0 at every age; PCP IV dextrose = D10W only
  • Febrile seizure: 3 months–6 years, fever, no other cause
  • Simple: whole body, under 15 min; still needs a doctor
  • Still seizing on arrival? Assume 10+ minutes

Airway, O₂, BVM if breathing is poor. Benzodiazepines: not BC EMR/PCP.
slides.say: A sleepy or confused child needs a glucose check every time, because low sugar is easy to fix. BC treats a blood glucose under four point zero the same at every age, and the PCP's IV dextrose is D10W only; glucagon is the back-up when you can't get an IV. A febrile seizure happens between three months and six years, with a fever and no other cause. A simple one is generalized and lasts under fifteen minutes; the child usually wakes quickly, but still needs a doctor. If the child is still seizing when you arrive, assume it's gone on at least ten minutes. Protect the airway, give oxygen, and bag if breathing is poor.
slides.sayZh: 嗜睡或意识混乱的孩子每次都要测血糖，因为低血糖很容易纠正。BC 各年龄一律按血糖低于四点零处理，PCP 的静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W；开不了静脉时用胰高血糖素兜底。热性惊厥发生在三个月到六岁之间，有发热，没有其他原因。单纯型是全身性的，不到十五分钟；孩子通常很快醒来，但仍需要医生评估。如果你到场时孩子还在抽，就当作已经抽了至少十分钟。保护气道、给氧，呼吸不足就球囊通气。

slides.title: Poisoning: one pill can kill
slides.body:
• More than half of exposures: children under 6
  • Toddlers explore: one product, small amounts
  • Teens: recreational or self-harm, often several drugs
  • Some adult pills can kill a toddler in 1–2 tablets
  • Check glucose; bring every bottle and container

No ipecac. Activated charcoal is not in BC EMR/PCP scope.
slides.say: More than half of poisonings happen in children under six. Toddlers explore with their mouths, usually swallowing one product in small amounts. Teenagers are different: recreational drug use or self-harm, often with several substances, and more dangerous. Some adult medicines, such as certain heart, blood pressure and diabetes pills, can kill a toddler with one or two tablets, so a child who looks fine on arrival isn't necessarily safe. Check the glucose, because alcohol, diabetes pills and beta blockers can drop it. Bring every bottle. Ipecac is no longer used, and activated charcoal isn't in BC's EMR or PCP scope.
slides.sayZh: 一半以上的中毒发生在六岁以下的孩子身上。幼儿用嘴探索世界，通常只吞下少量的单一东西。青少年不同：娱乐性用药或自伤，常常多种物质混合，也更危险。有些成人药，比如某些心脏药、降压药和降糖药，一两片就能要了幼儿的命，所以到场时看着没事的孩子不一定安全。测血糖，因为酒精、降糖药和 β 受体阻滞剂都会让血糖下降。所有药瓶都带上。吐根糖浆已经不用了，活性炭不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。

slides.title: Sudden infant death, and BRUE
slides.body:
SUID / SIDSBRUE
Whatsudden death under 1 year; SIDS stays unexplained after full investigationbrief, frightening episode, now resolved
Signsfound after sleep; lividity, stiffness, frothy fluidpale or blue, choking, apnea, floppy
Knowpeak 2–4 months; prone sleep, soft bedding, smokenot related to SIDS
Your rolefollow protocol; coroner; support familytransport every infant
slides.say: Sudden unexpected infant death, or SUID, is any sudden death under one year without an obvious cause. SIDS is the part that stays unexplained even after an autopsy and scene investigation. It peaks at two to four months; risks include sleeping face down, soft bedding and tobacco smoke. The baby is often found after a nap, sometimes with lividity, stiffness, or frothy fluid at the nose and mouth. Follow your protocol on resuscitation, notify the coroner or police as required, and note any signs of suffocation or abuse. Use the baby's name and offer real compassion. A BRUE, a brief resolved unexplained event, is a frightening episode that has passed, unrelated to SIDS. Transport every one.
slides.sayZh: 婴儿意外猝死（SUID）指一岁以下、没有明显原因的突然死亡。SIDS 是其中即使做了尸检和现场调查仍无法解释的那部分，高峰在二到四个月；危险因素包括趴着睡、软被褥和烟草烟雾。宝宝常在小睡后被发现，有时已有尸斑、僵硬，或口鼻有泡沫样液体。按规程决定是否复苏，按要求通知验尸官或警方，并留意有无窒息或虐待的迹象。叫宝宝的名字，真诚地表达同情。BRUE，即短暂已缓解的不明原因事件，是一次已经过去的惊吓性发作，与 SIDS 无关。每一个都要转运。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Fluid is weight-based: 20 mL/kg, not a standard bag
  • Suspected cardiogenic shock: small, slow, watch the lungs
  • Ondansetron: 2 mg PO (6 months–4 years), 4 mg (4+ years)
  • Dimenhydrinate: 1 mg/kg, max 50 mg; under 25 kg? contact the ER
  • ASA: not for children with viral symptoms
  • An IV attempt must never delay transport
slides.say: Here's what's new for you. Fluid is weight-based: twenty millilitres per kilogram, not a standard bag, and you reassess every time. If you suspect cardiogenic shock, give a small, slow bolus and watch the breathing and saturation. For vomiting, BC's ondansetron dose is two milligrams by mouth from six months to four years, and four milligrams from four years up; the monograph gives no dose under six months. Dimenhydrinate is one milligram per kilogram, up to fifty, and BC says contact the ER if the child appears to weigh under twenty-five kilograms. ASA is contraindicated in children with viral symptoms. And an IV attempt must never delay transport.
slides.sayZh: 这些是你的新内容。补液按体重：每公斤二十毫升，不是随手挂一袋，每次都要复评。怀疑心源性休克，就少量、慢慢给，并盯着呼吸和血氧。呕吐时，BC 昂丹司琼剂量是六个月到四岁口服二毫克，四岁及以上四毫克；专论没有给六个月以下的剂量。茶苯海明每公斤一毫克、最多五十毫克，BC 规定孩子看起来不到二十五公斤时要联系急诊室。有病毒症状的儿童禁用阿司匹林。而且开静脉绝不能耽误转运。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: one IV try, then IO; BC EMR/PCP: no IO
  • Book sugar cut-offs 2.2 / 3.3 and D25W; BC: < 4.0, D10W only
  • Book's seizure drugs (benzodiazepines): not BC EMR/PCP
  • Book's antidotes: mostly not BC drugs; charcoal out of scope
  • Child CPR: 15:2 with two rescuers; 30:2 always is adult-only
slides.say: Let's line up the book and BC. The book switches to an intraosseous needle after one failed IV; BC EMR and PCP scope has no IO. The book uses low-sugar cut-offs of two point two in newborns and three point three in other children, with D25W; BC treats anything under four point zero, at every age, and the only IV dextrose is D10W. The book's first-line seizure drugs are benzodiazepines, which aren't in BC's EMR or PCP scope. Activated charcoal is out of scope. And for child CPR with two rescuers, BC uses fifteen to two; thirty to two every time is the adult rule.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 对一下。书里静脉失败一次就改骨髓腔穿刺；BC 的 EMR 和 PCP 范围没有骨髓腔通路。书里低血糖界值是新生儿二点二、其他儿童三点三，并用 D25W；BC 各年龄一律低于四点零就处理，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。书里抽搐的一线药是苯二氮卓类，不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 范围内。活性炭也不在范围内。儿童双人 CPR，BC 用十五比二；「一律三十比二」是成人规则。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Children hold their BP, then crash: fast HR + slow refill = shock
  2. PCP fluid: 20 mL/kg en route, reassess; no IO; BGL < 4.0 → D10W
  3. Child CPR: 15:2 with two rescuers; HR < 60 with poor perfusion → CPR

Next: abuse, trauma, burns and children with special needs
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: children hold their blood pressure until late, so a fast heart rate, cool skin and slow refill already mean shock. Two: as a PCP, give twenty millilitres per kilogram en route and reassess, remember there's no IO in your BC scope, and treat a glucose under four point zero with D10W. Three: for child CPR in BC, two rescuers use fifteen to two, and you start compressions when the heart rate is under sixty with poor perfusion. Next lesson: child abuse, trauma, burns, and children with special health care needs. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，孩子会把血压撑到很晚，所以心率快、皮肤凉、再充盈慢就已经是休克。二，作为 PCP，途中按每公斤二十毫升补液并复评；记住你在 BC 的范围里没有骨髓腔通路；血糖低于四点零用 D10W。三，BC 儿童 CPR 双人用十五比二，心率低于六十且灌注差就开始按压。下节课讲儿童虐待、创伤、烧伤和有特殊医疗需求的儿童。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
